card: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning in CMake and marks functions, methods, and lambdas that unconditionally throw or abort with [[noreturn]]. It also qualifies bare abort and exit calls with the std namespace. This prevents compiler static analysis false positives, such as spurious missing-return warnings, and enforces consistent annotations on future non-returning functions.
changed_since_previous: Dropped dependency on #36087 along with the commits introducing AssertUnreachable(), the scripted diff replacing assert(false), and the assertion linter.
evidence: PR description notes: 'Missing [[noreturn]] attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556. Add missing attributes, and turn on compiler warnings.'
problem: Functions that never return without `[[noreturn]]` attributes can cause compiler static analysis false positives, such as spurious `-Wreturn-type` warnings. Without compiler warning enforcement, missing annotations are easily overlooked.

risk.why: Only adds compiler warning flags, non-returning function attributes, and std:: qualification with no changes to runtime behavior.

scope_notes: Small mechanical changes touching 20 files across interfaces, tests, fuzzing, Qt, RPC, and node init.
summary: Enables the `-Wmissing-noreturn` compiler warning flag in CMake and adds `[[noreturn]]` attributes to functions, methods, and lambdas that unconditionally throw or terminate. It also qualifies calls to `abort()`, `exit()`, and `_Exit()` with the `std::` namespace, and adds compiler pragmas in fuzzing code where non-returning behavior depends on build configuration.
